thread:
sam: Heads up — customer Echo reported a surge of short-answer hallucinations after we merged their LoRA into the 13B-compact int4 variant. Repro steps and small logs below, cc @anya @mike

anya: Ugh. Are these new hallucinations or just higher frequency of previous failures? Any sample prompts?

sam: New patterns. Mostly date/temporal confab on single-turn Q&A ("When did X happen?"). Repro on a local dedicated replica with int4 runtime. Quick sample: 
```
Prompt: "When was the Horizon release pushed to prod?"
Model (post-merge, int4): "Horizon was released on June 12, 2024."
Expected: Either correct date or "I don't know" / safe fallback. Customer logs show ~28% incorrect confident answers vs 4% before.
```

mike: Can you paste the LoRA merge command / merge config? Curious if scale/hyper mismatch introduced bias.

sam: We used the standard merge script: `merge_lora.py --base 13b-compact --lora echo_fin --alpha 32 --mode add` then quantized with `quantize_int4 --out 13b-compact-echomerge-int4` — no custom rescale.

jamie: Did we change tokenizer or pre-tokenization mapping when merging? Token shifts often cause subtle conditioning shifts.

sam: Tokenizer untouched — same vocab and tokenizer.json. I ran a quick token map diff, looks identical.

anya: Could be scale/alpha mismatch interacting with int4 kernel selection. Two quick checks: 1) run the merged model in float16 without quant to see if errors persist; 2) run eval pack with prompt perturbations to measure sensitivity. I'll queue both.

ci-bot: CI: queued job 4829 — "echo-finetune-compat/float16-smoke" — started on runner-11.

obs-bot: Observability: spike in log-prob entropy drop on those Q/A prompts around 2801234500; routing shows cache bypass due to merge.

mike: If float16 removes the regression, it's likely quantization interaction. If float16 still bad, the LoRA itself changed model priors. Sam, can you dump the topk logits and attention norms for a failing example (both pre-merge and post-merge)? small diffs in attention norm can explain hallucination.

sam: Pasted minimal diff output (truncated):
```
Pre-merge topk: [0.65,0.12,0.08,0.03]
Post-merge topk: [0.46,0.28,0.15,0.04]
Attention norm mean layer 23 pre: 0.87 post: 0.62
```

anya: Interesting — post-merge attention norms dropped, distribution flattened. That suggests the LoRA or merge alpha is dampening key/query magnitudes. Quantization could amplify that. Try re-merging with `--alpha 64` or apply per-layer rescale on late layers.

jamie: Also run the quick-eval pack with the customer's focused prompt set plus adversarial perturbations (typo/date-format variants). We should compute per-prompt calibration: confidence vs correctness. I'll prepare the pack.

ci-bot: CI: job 4829 completed — float16 smoke: PASSED (no regression in float16).

sam: float16 looks clean — failures only on int4. So quant path is the trigger.

mike: OK — path forward: 1) try remerge with higher alpha; 2) run quantizer with symmetric vs asymmetric scale options; 3) test per-layer clipping on kv cache. If remerge fixes it, record as recommended alpha for this customer's LoRA.

anya: I'll try remerge + quantize with `--quant-mode asymmetric --clip 0.02` and run the quick eval. If that passes, we should add a per-customer quant profile to Redwood Optimize for future pipelines.

sam: Running the two experiments now. ETA ~20m. If successful, we push a canary build behind a routing policy for Echo (canary 10% traffic).

jamie: Also log this as a potential guideline: "LoRA merges that reduce attention norms can interact badly with aggressive int4 kernels; prefer alpha>=48 or per-layer rescaling on late layers." I'll draft a short tip doc after we confirm.

obs-bot: Metric alert cleared: entropy drop back within baseline during the float16 run.

sam: Quick update — remerge with `--alpha 64` + asymmetric quant passed the customer's eval pack: incorrect confident answers dropped to 5%. Pushing canary build now.

mike: Nice. After canary, let's bake for 24h and then recommend adding a custom quant profile for Echo in Redwood Optimize.

anya: I'll open a tiny runbook and add the merge/quant knobs to the finetune onboarding checklist.

sam: Thanks team. I'll keep thread updated with canary metrics. :thumbsup:
